hook: A car's dashboard shows speed, but a car is also described by which way it is going and by how fast that is changing. Push the gas and the velocity changes; press the brake and it changes the other way; turn the wheel at a steady speed and it still changes. All three are acceleration.

prereq.q: A runner goes from x = +40 m to x = +10 m. What is her displacement?
prereq.why: Displacement = final − initial = 10 m − 40 m = −30 m.

options: The average of the two velocities
prereq.why: Δ always means "change in": final minus initial.

figure.caption: The acceleration points the same way as the change in velocity. Same direction as v: speeding up. Opposite to v: slowing down.

chain.cause: An object changes position over a time interval Δt
chain.effect: its average velocity is Δx/Δt, with the sign of the displacement

chain.cause: The time interval is made shorter and shorter
chain.effect: the average velocity approaches the instantaneous velocity at that moment

chain.cause: The velocity changes in size or in direction
chain.effect: the object has an acceleration, a = Δv/Δt, pointing the same way as Δv

chain.cause: The acceleration points the same way as the velocity
chain.effect: the object speeds up; if it points the opposite way, the object slows down

ideas: The object model treats a car or a ball as a point with a position: size, shape and inner parts are ignored.
Average velocity = Δx/Δt. It uses the displacement, so a round trip has zero average velocity. Average speed uses the distance.
Average acceleration = Δv/Δt, in m/s². Acceleration is any change in velocity: speeding up, slowing down or turning.
The sign of a alone does not tell you whether an object speeds up. Compare it with v: same sign, speeding up; opposite signs, slowing down.
An instantaneous value is the average over a very short interval. An object can have v = 0 at an instant and still be accelerating.

misconception.wrong: A negative acceleration means the object is slowing down, and an object at rest has no acceleration.
misconception.right: A negative acceleration only points in the negative direction. A cart rolling down a ramp (negative v) with a negative a speeds up. At the top of its path, the cart has v = 0 but its velocity is still changing, so a is not zero.

summary: Average velocity is displacement over time, Δx/Δt, and average acceleration is change in velocity over time, Δv/Δt. Acceleration is any change in velocity and points along Δv: with v, the object speeds up; against v, it slows down. Instantaneous values are averages over very short intervals.
